title: Y2K Live, Dead & Wounded
author: Peter S. Kastner (Aberdeen Group)
abstract: This four-slide Aberdeen Group deck classifies major enterprise platforms and application bases as likely "living," "dead," or "wounded" in the Year 2000 transition. It highlights IBM MVS, AS/400, AIX, HP-UX, Solaris, and Windows NT as likely survivors while flagging older IBM, HP 3000, Bull, Data General, Unisys, Wang, and legacy manufacturing environments as vulnerable or obsolete. A final slide reframes the taxonomy as a services-targeting guide by steering Y2K remediation effort toward attractive downstream customer segments and away from riskier or less desirable ones.
importance_rationale: The deck is a concise but historically useful snapshot of late-1990s Y2K platform triage and remediation-market positioning. Its value is more in capturing analyst framing and services targeting than in presenting original primary research.
relevance_rationale: The platform calls and customer-targeting lens remain useful for understanding how Y2K created migration and remediation opportunities across legacy enterprise estates. It also preserves a compact taxonomy of which platforms were seen as resilient versus endangered on the eve of 2000.
prescience_rationale: The deck was directionally prescient: platforms such as AS/400, AIX, Solaris, HP-UX, and Windows NT broadly remained viable, while systems such as IBM System/3X, HP 3000 MPE, and Data General Eclipse largely exited the mainstream. Even where the labels simplify complex installed bases, the overall survival taxonomy aged well.
